notable_absence.finding: Despite its title ('Add Synonyms with the Quick Editor') and its own '-quick' id, this page's BODY never once mentions the Quick Editor, Quick Mode, or any Quick-Editor-specific UI step - every sentence about the thesaurus, recursion boundary, scoring, Vector Search exclusion, and SQL++ integration is byte-identical to synonyms-search.md. The only Quick-Editor-specific content anywhere in this pair is the two outbound link targets. This is the same 'difference is entirely in the links, not the facts' shape already flagged on create-synonym-collection-docs-quick.json, and it is direct evidence AGAINST this page needing a separate id from search:synonyms-search - the split exists in the registry, but not in the documentation's own content.

cross_component_finding: REGISTRY FORK TENSION (full writeup; see also add-synonym-source-quick.json for the shorter cross-reference). Of this batch's three -quick/non-quick pairs, the two most textually different (add-synonym-source vs -quick: different UI steps, Analyzer vs Language field) were kept as ONE shared concept per this round's dispatch instructions. This pair - the two most textually IDENTICAL of the three, tied with create-synonym-collection-docs for near-duplication - ended up with TWO ids instead, purely because a concurrent sibling batch (server/8.0/search/create-quick-index.json) reached and minted search:synonyms-search-quick before this batch read either page. The inconsistency is not a judgement call this record is making; it is a fact about extraction order that reconciliation should see and resolve, most likely by folding search:synonyms-search-quick into search:synonyms-search (an aliasesTo-style merge) given how much stronger the identity evidence is here than for the pair that was kept apart.
